stories.title: Related-Led Group Advancing 494-Boca Raton Apartment Community
stories.excerpt: Related Group, PEBB Enterprises and BH Group have begun work on Broken Sound Residences, a 494-home luxury residential community that marks the first milestone in the transformation of the former Office Depot corporate campus in Boca Raton. Once complete, the 28-acre destination will blend residences, retail, wellness offerings and modern office space into a single project. Designed by MSA Architects and construction led by Balfour Beatty, Broken Sound Residences will offer three distinct residential offerings. Broken Sound Residences will pair more than 23,000 square feet of indoor amenities with over half an acre of outdoor gathering spaces. Amenities include two pool decks, private cabanas, hot tubs, a cold plunge, a pavilion bar, outdoor grilling stations and lounge areas. Nearby, there is an additional pool, jacuzzi and resident wine lounge. Inside amenities include a hidden speakeasy lounge, private dining room, golf simulator, coworking lounges, resident clubrooms and a fitness center. An Equinox fitness campus will be one of the first tenants at the development. The post Related-Led Group Advancing 494-Boca Raton Apartment Community appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Related Group, PEBB, BH Group begin 494-unit luxury apartments at former Office Depot HQ, Boca Raton.
Mixed-use transformation: residences, retail, wellness, office on 28 acres; Equinox fitness anchor committed.
23,000 sq ft indoor + 0.5 acre outdoor amenities; Balfour Beatty construction; completion timeline not specified.
stories.summary: Related-Led Group has begun construction on Broken Sound Residences, a 494-unit luxury apartment community anchoring the adaptive reuse of the former Office Depot corporate campus in Boca Raton on 28 acres. The mixed-use development will include retail, wellness facilities, modern office space, and extensive amenities including an Equinox fitness campus. Balfour Beatty is managing construction, with MSA Architects as designer.
stories.impact: South Florida office-to-residential conversions signal persistent weakness in corporate real estate demand and a pivot toward mixed-use density; successfully executed adaptive reuse with branded fitness anchor (Equinox) de-risks lease-up and justifies premium positioning in South Florida's competitive luxury market. Watch for absorption pace and rent pricing relative to new-build luxury comps in Boca Raton proper to gauge market acceptance of former office real estate.

stories.title: Get to Know the Broker: Jonathan Stein of Douglas Elliman
stories.excerpt: For Jonathan Stein, the best is yet to come. Stein, 43, joined the real estate game in 2015 after spending time in the private equity space and then going on the road with his best friend’s rock band, Phantogram, as the tour manager. Now, he runs the Jonathan Stein Team at Douglas Elliman. Stein oversees a group of eight brokers at the firm, which has worked on deals ranging from $1 million to over $15 million. When former New York Mets and current Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Zack Wheeler needed to sell his SoHo penthouse at 73 Wooster Street, Stein and team member Gavin Shiminski stepped in, helping the major leaguer sell the unit for $26 million. It was one of the five largest sales in New York City in July. The road to such a successful real estate career wasn’t easy, but Stein said real estate is an amalgamation of his favorite things: design, architecture, mixing different personalities, and working well with people. “I got into real estate the old fashioned way — my life blew up and I needed a new career,” he said. “I was waiting tables at a buddy’s restaurant looking for what was going to come next. A friend suggested real estate and I loved the idea.” Commercial Observer caught up with Stein in August for “Get to Know the Broker,” a series where we connect with residential brokers to learn more about what makes them tick. This conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Commercial Observer: What has been the biggest deal of your career? Jonathan Stein: I haven’t done it yet. Check back next year. What is your career Everest? Doing my own development project! What’s something you think people would be surprised to learn about you? I grew up on a farm in a town of 170 people. We raised cattle and pigs, and I showed pigs in 4-H as a kid to help earn money for college. What’s your go-to takeout order? Sushi from my neighborhood omakase spot. What TV show are you currently binging? “All Creatures Great and Small.” What is your silliest pet peeve? When
bullets: Jonathan Stein Team, Douglas Elliman NYC, handled $26M Zack Wheeler SoHo penthouse sale, top-5 NYC deal July.

stories.summary: Jonathan Stein, 43, runs an eight-broker team at Douglas Elliman specializing in high-end residential sales in New York City. His team recently brokered the $26 million sale of a SoHo penthouse for Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Zack Wheeler, one of the five largest residential sales in NYC in July. Stein entered real estate in 2015 after careers in private equity and music touring.

stories.title: Rejection and Change Are Constants in Residential Brokerage. Adapt.
stories.excerpt: When I decided to get my real estate license, it’s safe to say I had no idea what I was in for. The perception of real estate agents is not the reality. A lot of people assume it’s about the money, but, for me, it’s really all about building and nurturing relationships. I’ve closed many deals by focusing on what was best for my clients, even when it required extra flexibility and problem-solving on my end. I realized early on that half the battle was just being available and accessible, and that building trust and transparency from the first call is key. As a young agent in the industry, I didn’t come into real estate with many connections. Most of my circle wasn’t ready to purchase a home or hire an agent for a rental. I had to find my own path, generating leads organically. But, as a young agent, I was extremely motivated to do so, and I was ready to adapt if needed. Mackenzie Kyle. PHOTO: Courtesy Platinum Properties One of my first deals was in the Financial District. My client’s mom found my profile on RentHop and called me out of the blue. We spoke about her search, and she asked if I could show an apartment in an hour. I lived an hour away from the building at this time, so I quickly rushed over. After a day of last-minute tours, I helped them find an apartment they loved. Their daughter was fresh out of school, and they were nervous about her moving to New York City, but, with my guidance and reassurance, they felt confident that the apartment was the right choice. I didn’t know this deal would jump-start my entire career, but it did. Not only do I still have an amazing relationship with these clients and have helped them find multiple homes, I was also connected with so many amazing referral clients from them because of the superior level of service that I provided. Her first deal came from a cold RentHop inquiry; subsequent success relied on availability and trust-building.

stories.title: Podcast: Using AI to Make Better CRE Acquisition & Underwriting Decisions
stories.excerpt: Steven Song is the founder and CEO of Diald, an AI-powered decision intelligence platform for commercial real estate. Before founding Diald, Steven worked on both the investing and development sides of real estate, and built his career across architecture and urban planning, training at Carnegie Mellon and the University of Pennsylvania. He was a founding principal at SCAAA, a global strategy, planning, and design firm, and is a partner at Axle Companies, a family office focused on real estate investment and social impact ventures. Steven is based in Los Angeles. stories.title: Machine Investment Group Closes Second Fund at Hard Cap of $350M
stories.excerpt: Machine Investment Group, LP, a New York City-based real estate investment platform focused on opportunistic, distressed and special situations across the U.S., reached the final close of Machine Real Estate Fund II, the firm’s second flagship investment vehicle. Fund II reached its $350 million hard cap in primary commitments and has raised an additional $120 million in co-investments to date. Fund II received support from a diverse group of new and returning institutional investors, including public and private pension funds, endowments, foundations, family offices and private investors. Fund II exceeded Machine’s debut fund, Machine Real Estate Fund I, which closed in 2022 with $246 million in primary commitments and $208 million in co-investments. “We are humbled by the support of our investment partners, including both returning Fund I investors and a number of new institutional relationships, which allowed us to reach our hard cap for Fund II,” said Eric Rosenthal, co-founder and managing partner of Machine Investment Group. “Reaching our hard cap in what continues to be a challenging fundraising environment, particularly for middle market managers pursuing a diversified strategy, is a milestone we do not take for granted.” Representative Fund II investments include a special situations powered land investment in Pennsylvania, a distressed 539-unit residential property in downtown San Jose, a 229-unit senior housing property on Long Island acquired out of a distressed situation, a recently developed 1.3 million square foot industrial park in Phoenix and a strategic capital investment in a publicly traded company being repositioned as a powered land and data center development platform. The post Machine Investment Group Closes Second Fund at Hard Cap of $350M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Machine Investment Group closes Fund II at $350M hard cap + $120M co-investments; Fund I was $246M (2022).
Focus: opportunistic, distressed, special situations real estate across U.S.; LP base: pensions, endowments, families, funds.
42% AUM growth Fund I→II; capital continues flowing to middle-market distressed despite challenging fundraising environment.
stories.summary: Machine Investment Group, a NYC-based real estate investment platform, closed Machine Real Estate Fund II at its $350 million hard cap in primary commitments, plus $120 million in co-investments. Fund II exceeds Fund I (closed 2022 with $246M primary + $208M co-investments) and received support from diverse institutional and private investors including pension funds, endowments, and family offices.
stories.impact: Capital availability for distressed and special-situations multifamily assets remains strong despite a challenging fundraising environment; growth in opportunistic fund AUM suggests institutional appetite for value-add and repositioning plays. Expect continued downward pressure on cap rates for stabilized assets and floor pricing for distressed deals as competitive capital chases opportunities.

stories.title: Jamison CEO Jaime Lee Joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director
stories.excerpt: Kennedy Wilson said Wednesday that Jaime Lee has joined the firm as senior managing director of capital markets and real estate investments. Most recently CEO of Los Angeles-based Jamison, Lee joins Kennedy Wilson as the firm continues to expand its investment management platform and deepen relationships with institutional and private capital partners.   In her new role, Lee will help lead capital formation initiatives, strengthen relationships with institutional investors and strategic partners, and help drive investment opportunities across Kennedy Wilson’s global real estate platform.  “Jaime brings an exceptional combination of investment expertise, operational experience and longstanding relationships across both the private and public sectors,” said William McMorrow, chairman and CEO of Kennedy Wilson. “As we continue to grow our investment management platform and expand our capital formation capabilities, Jaime’s proven ability to build partnerships, identify opportunities and navigate complex transactions will be invaluable.” Lee joins Kennedy Wilson following more than 20 years at Jamison, where she helped transform the company into one of Southern California’s largest privately held real estate owners and developers.  The post Jamison CEO Jaime Lee Joins Kennedy Wilson as Senior Managing Director appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Jaime Lee, former Jamison CEO (20+ years), joins Kennedy Wilson as senior MD of capital markets.
Role: capital formation, institutional investor relations, investment opportunities across KW's global platform.
C-suite talent move signals KW expansion of investment management and capital-raising capabilities.
stories.summary: Kennedy Wilson announced that Jaime Lee, former CEO of LA-based Jamison (where she spent over 20 years), has joined as senior managing director of capital markets and real estate investments. In her new role, Lee will lead capital formation, strengthen institutional relationships, and drive investment opportunities across Kennedy Wilson's global platform.
stories.impact: Talent migration from a mid-market developer (Jamison) to a larger, publicly-traded capital manager (Kennedy Wilson) signals consolidation in real estate management and a shift toward institutional scale. Lee's appointment strengthens KW's ability to compete for institutional LP capital, which may increase competitive pressure on mid-market developers for deal access and capital partners.

stories.title: Developer Iadisernia Lands Mezz Loan to Finish Hallandale, Fla., Condo Tower
stories.excerpt: More than a year after landing a $112 million loan to complete a mixed-use project in Hallandale Beach, Fla., developer Giuseppe Iadisernia has secured yet more debt. Cottonwood Group supplied a $50 million mezzanine loan for a 250-unit condo tower within the 10-acre Oasis mixed-use development at 1000 East Hallandale Beach Boulevard, about a mile west of the beach, the L.A.-based lender announced Wednesday. Construction is expected to be completed next year. Emile Schachter’s WD Capital Group brokered the debt. A representative for the lender has yet to provide figures regarding condo sales. Last year, S3 Capital had provided the $112 million construction loan for the 25-story tower, considered the last phase of the mixed-use broader development. Prices range from $580,000 and $3.5 million. Just last month, the first condo tower, also a 250-unit, 25-story high-rise, secured a temporary certificate of occupancy up to the 12th floor. The development includes a commercial portion with about 35,000 square feet of office space and 60,000 square feet of retail space, which was completed in 2024. Since the pandemic, when northerners flocked to Florida, Hallandale has been going upscale. In 2024, Witkoff and PPG Development nabbed a $273 million construction loan for a 20-story condo and hotel building within their exclusive Shell Bay golf country club. But some projects have struggled. In March, Monroe Capital sued PPG Development’s Ari Pearl and the principals of BH3 over a $70 million loan tied to Hallandale Beach Residences, The Real Deal reported. The lender alleged the developer stopped making payments in February. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Giuseppe Iadisernia secures $50M mezzanine loan (Cottonwood Group) for 250-unit condo tower, Hallandale Beach, Fla.
Oasis mixed-use development; 25-story tower; unit prices $580K–$3.5M; construction completion targeted next year.
S3 Capital provided $112M construction loan last year; condo sales metrics not disclosed; mezz signals refinancing/capital stack pressure.
stories.summary: Developer Giuseppe Iadisernia secured a $50 million mezzanine loan from Cottonwood Group for a 250-unit condo tower within the Oasis mixed-use development in Hallandale Beach, Florida. The 25-story tower is part of a 10-acre mixed-use project with unit prices ranging from $580,000 to $3.5 million and is expected to complete construction next year. S3 Capital provided the initial $112 million construction loan.
stories.impact: South Florida condo development capital markets showing stress: mezz financing is typically a sign of either aggressive leverage (original construction loan insufficient) or slower-than-modeled pre-sales. Monitor Hallandale pre-sales absorption and the first tower's lease-up (250 units already secured COO to 12th floor) to gauge market-driven demand vs. construction-driven supply in the rental and for-sale segments. Watch for similar mezz closings as a proxy for stretched capital stacks in condo-heavy markets.

stories.title: Century 21 Redevelopment Adds Burlington, National Grocer to Tenant Roster
stories.excerpt: MCB Real Estate, an institutional commercial real estate investment management firm and developer with nationwide holdings, and Osiris Ventures, an urban retail-focused investment firm, have secured leases with two major retail brands at Century Marketplace, the $130-million mixed-use redevelopment of the 14-lot Century 21 department store assemblage at 458 86th St. in Brooklyn’s Bay Ridge neighborhood. A national grocery anchor has signed a lease at the property, becoming the first national grocer to serve the immediate Southwest Brooklyn trade area. National designer-discount retailer Burlington has also signed on, and together the two leases total 60,112 square feet. With these additions, the 120,000-square-foot Century Marketplace is now 65% pre-leased. “Century Marketplace demonstrates MCB Real Estate’s ability to execute complex structuring while delivering high quality, attractive retail to dense markets,” said MCB principal Drew Gorman. “By bringing together a nationally recognized specialty grocery anchor, and top national retailers like Burlington, we are reigniting a well-known commercial corridor and unlocking long term value for Southwest Brooklyn.” The post Century 21 Redevelopment Adds Burlington, National Grocer to Tenant Roster appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MCB Real Estate/Osiris Ventures: Burlington and national grocer sign leases at Century Marketplace, Brooklyn Bay Ridge.
120,000 sq ft mixed-use redevelopment; 65% pre-leased; two tenants total 60,112 sq ft; $130M project.
First national grocer to serve Southwest Brooklyn trade area; retail anchor fills signal strong neighborhood retail demand.
stories.summary: MCB Real Estate and Osiris Ventures have secured leases with Burlington (discount retailer) and a major national grocery anchor at Century Marketplace, a $130 million mixed-use redevelopment of the former Century 21 department store at 458 86th Street in Brooklyn's Bay Ridge. The two tenants occupy 60,112 square feet combined, bringing the 120,000-square-foot project to 65% pre-leased. The grocer is the first national grocery operator to serve the immediate Southwest Brooklyn trade area.
stories.impact: Successful retail anchor leasing in Brooklyn mixed-use development signals renewed confidence in urban retail and neighborhood grocer viability post-pandemic. The first-national-grocer claim suggests densifying Brooklyn submarkets (Bay Ridge, Sunset Park corridor) are attractive to operators previously underserved—potential pull for multifamily by improving neighborhood amenity profile and walkability, justifying higher rents. Watch for similar urban grocery openings as leading indicators of mixed-use mixed-income neighborhood strengthening.

stories.title: Multi-Tenant Corona del Mar Retail Sells Above Asking Price
stories.excerpt: Coastal Commercial and Marcus & Millichap arranged the $13.7-million sale of 2515 E. Coast Highway, a prominent multi-tenant retail property located in Corona del Mar. The transaction was represented by Nathan Holthouser of Coastal Commercial and Ron Duong of Marcus & Millichap. The offering generated significant interest from the Orange County investment community, attracting more than 10 offers and multiple rounds of competitive bidding. Prospective buyers consisted primarily of high-net-worth private investors with ties to Orange County. Ultimately, the property sold for $700,000 above its asking price. “The response to this offering was exceptional, but I think sophisticated investors quickly recognized the underlying value of the real estate,” said Holthouser. “You have incredible frontage along Pacific Coast Highway, approximately 20 onsite parking spaces — which is extremely difficult to replicate in Corona del Mar — and a collection of mostly smaller commercial spaces that lend themselves well to maximizing rents over time.” The post Multi-Tenant Corona del Mar Retail Sells Above Asking Price appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: 2515 E. Coast Highway, Corona del Mar, sold for $13.7M, $700K above asking; 10+ offers, competitive bidding.
Multi-tenant retail; PCH frontage; ~20 parking spaces; smaller commercial spaces optimized for rent maximization.
High-net-worth Orange County investor base; strong coastal retail fundamentals and scarcity premium for parking/frontage.
stories.summary: A multi-tenant retail property at 2515 E. Coast Highway in Corona del Mar sold for $13.7 million, $700,000 above its asking price. The transaction attracted more than 10 offers and multiple rounds of competitive bidding, primarily from high-net-worth Orange County private investors. The property features prominent PCH frontage, approximately 20 onsite parking spaces, and smaller commercial spaces suited to rent growth.
stories.impact: Coastal retail real estate in Orange County experiencing strong investor demand and upward price momentum, driven by scarcity of parking and highway visibility in premium submarkets. This signals healthy retail fundamentals in affluent coastal CA markets and suggests multifamily developers in similar OC submarkets can justify higher rents if adjacent retail/amenity profile strengthens. Limited supply of parking-inclusive commercial sites in Corona del Mar is a persistent constraint and may inflate land costs for any mixed-use residential redevelopment.
